title: Crassulacean Acid Metabolism (CAM Pathway)
topic: Temporal Separation, Nocturnal Stomata Opening, Vacuolar Malic Acid Storage, & Xeric Adaptation
topics: CAM Photosynthesis Overview (Pineapple, Agave, Cactus, Opuntia, Sedum)
Temporal Separation of Carbon Fixation vs C4 Spatial Separation
Nighttime Reactions: Scotoactive Stomatal Opening & PEPCase Malate Synthesis
Nocturnal Acidification: Vacuolar Storage of Malic Acid
Daytime Reactions: Stomatal Closure, Malate Decarboxylation, & RuBisCO C3 Fixation
Extreme Water-Use Efficiency in Xeric Environments
quickSummary: CAM plants (Crassulaceae, Cacti, Pineapple) survive extreme arid environments through temporal separation of carbon fixation. At night, scotoactive stomata open to minimize transpiration; PEPCase fixes CO2 into malate, stored as malic acid in large vacuoles (nocturnal acidification). During the day, stomata remain tightly closed; malic acid leaves the vacuole and is decarboxylated to release CO2, which is fixed by RuBisCO via the C3 Calvin cycle using light-generated ATP and NADPH.

conceptBreakdown.title: 7. CAM Temporal Separation Framework

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: CAM = Temporal separation (Night: Stomata open, PEPCase, Malic acid in vacuole; Day: Stomata closed, Decarboxylation, RuBisCO C3).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
CAM TEMPORAL SEPARATION
                                      │
         ┌────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                         ▼
   NIGHTTIME MECHANISM                                       DAYTIME MECHANISM
   ├── Stomata OPEN (Prevents transpiration)                 ├── Stomata CLOSED (Prevents water loss)
   ├── $\text{CO}_2$ fixed by PEPCase ──► OAA ──► Malate      ├── Malate leaves vacuole ──► Decarboxylated
   └── Malic Acid stored in **Large Vacuoles**                └── High internal $\text{CO}_2$ fixed by RuBisCO ($C_3$)
conceptBreakdown.content: Crassulacean Acid Metabolism (**CAM**) operates in succulent desert plants (*Cacti, Agave, Pineapple, Opuntia, Sedum*) to achieve maximal water-use efficiency.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 7.1 Diurnal Biochemical Dynamics
conceptBreakdown.title: 7.1 Diurnal Biochemical Dynamics
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
CAM PATHWAY CYCLE
                        
   NIGHT:  HCO₃⁻ + PEP ──[PEPCase]──► Malate ──► Vacuolar Storage (Malic Acid)
   
   DAY:    Malic Acid ──► Cytosol ──► Decarboxylation ──► CO₂ ──► RuBisCO ($C_3$) ──► Glucose
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Night (Scotoactive Phase)**: Stomata open when relative humidity is higher and temperatures are lower. $\text{CO}_2$ is converted to $\text{HCO}_3^-$ and fixed by **PEPCase** to form oxaloacetate, reduced to malate, and transported across the tonoplast into the central vacuole as **Malic Acid** (causing nighttime tissue acidification).
• **Day (Photoactive Phase)**: Stomata remain closed to prevent transpiration water loss. Malate exits the vacuole into the cytosol and is decarboxylated, releasing high internal $\text{CO}_2$ to be fixed by **RuBisCO in the Calvin ($C_3$) cycle** using solar ATP and NADPH.
